Pinterest Setup, Pins and Strategy

Pinterest Business Account Setup Checklist

By Marie Glow StudioPublished August 3, 2026Updated September 26, 2026

Bookmark this one: it's meant to be worked through in order, not read once. This Pinterest business account setup checklist has eight steps, from creating or converting the account to reviewing analytics after 30 days, and each step builds on the one before it.

What is on the Pinterest business account setup checklist?

Work through these eight steps in order:

  1. Create the business account, or convert your existing account to one.
  2. Give the profile a name that states what you offer.
  3. Write a bio in plain, searchable language.
  4. Connect and verify your website.
  5. Create five to ten boards around real business topics.
  6. Title and describe each board with real search terms.
  7. Publish your first 10 to 15 Pins, each linked to a specific page.
  8. Review your analytics after 30 days to confirm what is working.

What should you have ready before you start?

Have four things to hand: a plain description of what you sell or teach, the page on your website each Pin will lead to, your brand colors, fonts and logo, and a handful of clear photos. Having these ready keeps the profile, boards and first Pins consistent, and it stops you stalling halfway through.

Why does the order of the checklist matter?

Because each step gives the next one something to point to. The profile tells people what the account is about, the website gives Pins a destination, and the boards need both before they can be named well. Reverse the order and you end up renaming and redoing work.

The order also guards against four setup mistakes: publishing before the website is ready, creating too many vague boards at once, keeping a clever profile name that hides your offer, and leaving old personal content mixed into the business account.

How do you finish steps 1 to 3, the account and profile?

Choose a business account, then write the name and bio for a customer rather than for yourself. The name should state what you offer, and the bio should use words a shopper would search. The full guide to setting up a Pinterest business account explains the reasoning, and Pinterest profile SEO covers the name and bio in detail.

What counts as done for the website step?

Step 4 is done when your website is connected and verified, and every page you plan to link to is live and ready for visitors. Pause at this step if the site is not ready, because every Pin you publish needs a working page behind it.

What counts as done for the board steps, 5 and 6?

Five to ten boards exist, and each one has a title and a short description written with the phrase a customer would search. A label like "Sparkle & Shine" fails this test, while a plain topic name passes. Aim for boards specific enough that you could explain in one sentence what belongs on each. Pinterest board SEO covers titles, descriptions and grouping.

How many Pins should you publish first, and where should they link?

Publish 10 to 15 Pins first, and link each one to a specific page that delivers what the Pin promises. Give every Pin a clear title, a description and a board that fits. The guide to SEO-friendly Pinterest Pin titles and the guide to designing Pinterest Pins cover the writing and the look.

When should you review your analytics?

After 30 days, look at what the account has done and note which topics and Pins earned outbound clicks. Then decide what to make more of. Expect the first numbers to be uneven, and remember that the checklist gives you a stronger foundation rather than a guarantee: results still vary with niche, competition and consistency.

Can you hand the checklist off?

Yes. Pinterest Business Account Setup and SEO Optimization from Marie Glow Studio covers the same ground. It creates or optimizes the business account, writes an SEO-focused profile, builds board strategy across up to 10 boards, makes 10 custom Pins and adds a 30 day launch plan.

No consultation is needed: you check out, complete an intake form, and the work starts once your information and access are received. It is delivered 10 to 15 business days after that, and ongoing posting is a separate service.

Frequently asked questions

When should I review my Pinterest analytics after setup?

Review them after 30 days to confirm what is working. Note which topics and Pins earned outbound clicks, and plan the next round around them.

Do I have to follow the setup checklist in order?

As far as you can, yes, because each step supports the next: profile first, then the website connection, then boards, then Pins.
